page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v6 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Dav6 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 32 dedicated virtual CPUs, mapped from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32as_v6 demonstrates strong single-core and memory performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier, while the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores are in the strong top 25% tier. Memory performance is also notable, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%. However, multi-core raw compute and memory bandwidth tests, such as stress-ng multi-core and uncached read/write operations, fall into the average middle 50% category. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 extensions and cryptographic acceleration, which contribute to its strong performance in encryption tests and small-model LLM inference.

The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, making this instance unsuitable for heavy local database caching or GPU-accelerated machine learning training. However, its balanced resource profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for general-purpose enterprise workloads. The combination of strong single-thread performance and a balanced memory-to-core ratio makes the D32as_v6 well-suited for web serving, application servers, software compilation, text and image processing, and moderate database operations utilizing network-attached Premium Storage.
